lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Systems of Linear Equations and Inequalities
lessonRef.focus: interpreting and verifying a system solution in context
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: interpreting and verifying a system solution in context

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: Is the point (-3, -5) in the solution region of -3x + 4y ≤ -2?
choices: No; substituting gives -11, which is greater than -2.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.
Yes; substituting gives -11 ≤ -2.
Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 3 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.
The new system is equivalent only when 3 is 1.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  2x − 6y = 10
  3x − 6y = 13
choices: exactly one solution
infinitely many solutions
no solution
exactly two solutions

items.prompt: Is the point (2, -8) in the solution region of -7x − 1y ≤ 9?
choices: Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.
Yes; substituting gives -6 ≤ 9.
No; substituting gives -6, which is greater than 9.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 5 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system is equivalent only when 5 is 1.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  1x − 4y = 3
  4x − 16y = 17
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
